issues.legal_issue: A newly enacted reassessment power does not apply retrospectively to reopen an estate-duty assessment completed before it took effect absent express or necessarily implied retroactive intent.
material_facts: The estate-duty assessment was completed before the new reassessment provision came into force.
After that provision came into force, the revenue authority issued a notice seeking to reopen the completed assessment because property was said to have escaped duty.

The former provision chiefly authorized rectification of mistakes, while the new provision addressed property escaping assessment; the Court found their powers materially different despite some overlap concerning omitted property.
issues.conclusion: The new reassessment provision was not retrospective, and reopening the completed assessment under it was unlawful.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 56–65 of the Estate Duty Act, 1953, as amended by the Estate Duty (Amendment) Act, 1958, the former section 62 concerned rectification of mistakes, whereas the substituted section 59 concerned property escaping assessment and conferred a materially different power. Section 59 was analogous to section 34 of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1922 and section 147 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Retrospective operation must be expressly stated or necessarily implied; absent that, later legislation does not interfere with vested rights, and a completed assessment cannot be reopened unless the statute permits it. The Court relied on Controller of Estate Duty, West Bengal v. Smt. Ila Das and Others, [1981] 132 I.T.R. 720.

predicates.estate_duty_reassessment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an attempt by a revenue authority to reassess estate duty.
predicates.assessment_completed_before_new_power_ef: The revenue authority completed the assessment before the new reassessment power took effect.
predicates.new_power_materially_differs_from_prior_: The new reassessment power addressed a materially different situation from the earlier power to correct assessment mistakes.
predicates.retroactive_intent_expressed_or_necessar: The legislation expressly stated, or necessarily implied, that the new power applied retrospectively.
predicates.reopening_of_completed_assessment_is_unl: The revenue authority may not reopen the completed assessment under the new power.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty reassessment proceeding concerns an assessment completed before a materially different new reassessment power took effect, and retrospective intent was neither expressed nor necessarily implied, the completed assessment cannot be reopened under that power.
